decision_reason: The frozen 0.0.2a1 wheel predates V3-01 (no saimail/custody.py, no identity schema v2, no --custody/os-store CLI). Its external proof binds exactly those bytes. The current checkout is not externally verified, and V3-01 is intended for distribution, so the frozen candidate may be published only as the pre-V3-01 historical alpha, and the current capability needs a new candidate identity.

current_source_delta.note: The checkout contains saimail/custody.py and os-store custody; no distributable artifact of the current checkout exists, and none is externally verified.

version_decision.intentional_difference: The checkout still declares 0.0.2a1 although it contains post-freeze V3-01 code. The version string is not artifact identity (D-052): the frozen wheel is identified by its SHA-256, and the next candidate gate (D2) owns the version-surface bump to 0.0.2a2 when it builds and freezes the new wheel.

custody_default_decision.rationale: The zero-required-dependency core install contract is documented (pyproject.toml, README, D-052, D-053); an os-store default would put keyring on the ordinary path or force a silent degradation that spec/20 excludes. OS-store backend evidence exists on Windows only (WinVaultKeyring classification and one disposable smoke); the external proof environment is Linux, so a protected default would make an unproven platform path primary. An explicit-choice requirement would break the documented init compatibility without an observed need.
next_candidate_requirements: keep raw as the documented default and os-store as the explicit opt-in
keep the base-path install contract free of required runtime dependencies
carry the raw-custody warning on the first-run surface without changing behavior
re-evaluate the default only when a second supported platform has verified OS-store backend evidence
